b26449375a.q: How can healthcare practices use AI to replace recruiter fees and build internal hiring capacity?
b26449375a.a: You can leverage AI to streamline the sourcing phase while you sleep or work on competing business priorities, then implement a system that works smarter rather than harder. This allows you to bring the recruiting process fully in-house and only use agency recruiting spend on very difficult roles that haven't worked through that system due to location, expectations, experience, or niche requirements. For 95% of your roles, AI-driven systems should work and allow you to keep that money in-house.
b26449375a.e: Using AI to Replace Recruiters for Hiring in Healthcare
b26449375a.rq: AI is going to replace recruiting eventually, and if you have a good grip on how to do that, then you're not behind the mark.

7fc532ca30.q: What is the difference between hunting and farming in healthcare recruiting?
7fc532ca30.a: Hunting involves finding people who are not actively applying on job boards—proactively sourcing candidates. Farming involves processing resumes from people who have already applied. Most HR professionals only farm, while agency recruiters hunt. Internal recruiters are capable of hunting and can be incentivized to do so without continuously paying 20% of salary fees.

b2946aaa02.q: Why is timing critical in healthcare recruiting and hiring clinicians?
b2946aaa02.a: Everything in recruiting and finding good talent, clinicians, and support staff is about timing because it is a candidate-driven market, meaning there are more jobs than there are candidates. Being competitive requires not only offering attractive positions but also finding people and promoting your brand effectively to attract better candidates.
